# How to Build a Markdown Blog with Next.js 15: The Complete Guide
This is exactly how this blog is built. Let me show you how to create your own **Next.js 15 App Router markdown blog** with a complete **developer blog setup** .

## TL;DR
If you're short on time, here's the stack:
* **Next.js 15 App Router** for static generation
* **Markdown files** in a `_posts/` folder for content
* **gray-matter** to parse frontmatter metadata
* **remark + remark-gfm** to convert markdown to HTML
* **Tailwind CSS** for styling (optional but recommended)

...

## Project Structure
```
├── api.ts               # Functions to read posts
└── markdownToHtml.ts    # Markdown processor
interfaces/
└── post.ts              # TypeScript types
```

...

## Step 1: Set Up Your Next.js Project
* **gray-matter** : Parses YAML frontmatter from markdown files
* **remark** : Core markdown processor
* **remark-gfm** : Adds GitHub-flavored markdown (tables, strikethrough, task lists)
* **remark-rehype** : Converts markdown AST to HTML AST
* **rehype-slug** : Adds IDs to headings (for anchor links)

...

## Step 3: Create the Blog API
1. `getPostSlugs()` reads all filenames from `_posts/`
2. `getPostBySlug()` reads a specific file, parses its frontmatter with gray-matter, and returns a typed `Post` object
3. `getAllPosts()` gets all posts and sorts them by date (newest first)
4.

...

## Step 5: Create Your First Post
// Generate static pages for all posts at build time export async function generateStaticParams ( ) {
const  posts =  getAllPosts ();
return  posts. map ( ( post ) =>  ({  slug : post. slug  }));
}

...

```

**Key patterns here:**

* `generateStaticParams()` pre-renders all blog posts at build time
* `generateMetadata()` creates unique SEO metadata for each post
```

`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
* [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
* [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
* [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)

or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding
Layouts or Pages are generated.During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.`generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.

...

# Parameters
## Multiple Dynamic Segments
```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
export function generateStaticParams() {
  return [
    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
  ]
}

// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
```

...

## Examples
### Prerendering
#### All paths at build time
```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
export async function generateStaticParams() {
  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())

  return posts.map((post) => ({
    slug: post.slug,
  }))
}
```

...

#### All paths at runtime
```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
export async function generateStaticParams() {
  return []
}
```
> **Good to know:**You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.

...

### With Route Handlers
```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
export async function generateStaticParams() {
  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
}

export async function GET(request, { params }) {
  const { id } = await params
  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
```

results.title: Purpose of generateStaticParams in next js, and is it worth it?
excerpts:
# Purpose of generateStaticParams in next js, and is it worth it? #73959
## baranelitez Dec 16, 2024
|### Summary
I've been reading the next.js docs, and there are two things that puzzle me about the `generateStaticParams` .
**[#1](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/1)** : 1st thing that puzzles me is the paragraph at https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes .

...

**[#2](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/2)** I understand that it also generates the route before a request has been made as well. But that's what makes me wonder.. I'll try explaining with an example:
**Case 1:** For our blog posts, we **don't** use SSG ( `generateStaticParams` ):
As far as I know, once a dynamic route like /blog/posts/[slug] is hit, the content is generated at request time, stored in the "Full Route Cache" which is persistent, and then sent to the visitor's browser. Any visits from now on, whether it be 5 mins later or a month, will be sent from this cache.

...

Now let's say in Case 1, we had all of our blog posts visited by previous visitors. And that will cause every rendered blogpost page to be stored in the "Full Route Cache", which effectively brings it to the same state with Case 2.

...

## Replies: 1 comment · 2 replies
### icyJoseph Dec 16, 2024
I think, `getStaticPaths` , sums it up best. You can pre-render a bunch of pages upfront, and then decide whether or not you want this to be a closed set, or not.
If its a closed set, you can serve both the content, and 404's such for non existing content, right away. No on-demand needed.

...

I think this section of the migration, can help you: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/upgrading/app-router-migration to correlate both `getStaticPaths` and `generateStaticParams` , to actually gain insight into whats the problem the framework is trying to solve with them.
| Having written all of this now, I think the claim, `faster generation times` , while certainly true, it is a bit of a catch-22. Since in App Router, you fetch the data where you need it. And there's no way to pass data from `generateStaticParams` to the page, you'd have to call the same data endpoint in both.

...

So far, we’ve explored **Static Rendering** and **Dynamic Rendering** in Next.js. Now, it’s time to unlock the **best of both worlds** — using `**generateStaticParams**` to pre-render dynamic routes **at build time** .
Press enter or click to view image in full size
This technique gives you lightning-fast load times for pages with known paths **(like featured products or popular blog posts)** while still supporting dynamic routes for less frequent or unknown content.

## 🤔 What Is generateStaticParams?
> In simple terms, `**generateStaticParams**` is a special **build-time function** that works with **dynamic route segments** in Next.js.
It allows you to define which dynamic pages should be statically generated during the build — providing a **performance boost** by avoiding on-demand rendering for known pages.

## 🛍️ Real Example: Featured Products
Let’s say we’re building a product listing site with a detail page for each product.

### 📁 Folder Structure:
```
app/  
└── products/  
    ├── page.tsx            → Product listing page  
    └── [id]/  
        └── page.tsx        → Dynamic product details
```
